text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — elevated OOM/crash rate for runtime-service (eu-west-2 pool). Auto-opened INC-2026-224. Affected: 3 containers across nodes gpu-09,gpu-12,gpu-15. Symptoms: gradual GPU memory climb -> CUBLAS/CUDA_ALLOC failures -> container restart. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-224 :rotating_light:

sarah.k: picking this up. I see a steady mem increase on gpu-09 over last ~14h. Not a single spike, more like a slow drip.

ajay: same on gpu-12 logs show repeated: 
```
2026-03-15T02:12:34Z runtime-service[pid=4210]: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
2026-03-15T02:12:34Z runtime-service[pid=4210]: cublasAlloc failed: 2
2026-03-15T02:12:34Z kernel: container exited with status 137
```

marco: interestingly the node-level rq stats show steady KV cache 'slot' growth, fragmentation > 0.85 on all three nodes. Could be paged-attn allocator leak.

sarah.k: markers: high page-fault churn on the paged allocator, GC doesn't reclaim because pages marked sticky due to in-flight KV refs. suspected regression after rollout 2026-03-10 (runtime v3.4.1).

ajay: i rolled back runtime to 3.4.0 on gpu-12 via canary and mem climb stopped after ~30m. gpu-09 and gpu-15 still on 3.4.1.

ops-aya: can we trigger conservative eviction/compaction on affected nodes? there is a kvcache-sweep endpoint.

marco: yes — endpoint: POST /admin/kvcache/compact?level=aggressive. hitting that now for gpu-09.

marco: results: compact started, freed ~1.2GB but mem still creeping. suspect fragmentation (many small allocations) that compact can't fully coalesce.

sarah.k: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable 3.4.1 pool traffic -> route to 3.4.0 variant 2) run aggressive kv compaction on affected nodes 3) coordinate rolling restart if compaction doesn't arrest growth 4) reduce per-request max_seq_len to 2048 for EU to lower pressure.

lee: doing traffic flip now, routing EU inference -> runtime-3.4.0. ETA ~2m.

oncall-bot: ROUTE UPDATE — traffic switch complete for pool eu-west-2 -> runtime-3.4.0.

ajay: post-flip: gpu-12 mem stabilized as expected. gpu-09 still climbing; compaction freed some but not enough. planning restart of runtime container on gpu-09 to reclaim device allocations.

sarah.k: agree. marco will coordinate restart. aim for rolling restarts with readiness probes to avoid cascade.

marco: restarting runtime on gpu-09 (graceful drain, 30s drain).

marco: restart done. node came back, mem baseline lower. Monitoring for 20m.

ajay: cuda errors stopped on gpu-09 after restart, gpu-15 still showing leak.

ops-aya: starting compaction & then restart on gpu-15.

ops-aya: compaction reclaimed ~800MB then container restart. Post-restart mem baseline OK.

sarah.k: consolidation: root cause likely paged-attention allocator fragmentation + a regression in 3.4.1 that changed KV ref lifecycle, preventing background reclamation. small allocations accumulate -> fragmentation -> effective usable GPU memory drops until OOM.

lee: customer impact: we saw a spike in 504s and retries for embeddings/chat generation in EU region between 01:30-03:10 UTC. Error budget hit: ~5% of requests experienced a failure or retry. No data exfiltration; requests failed/timeout only.

marco: created follow-up ticket: RT-2026-881 'paged-attn KV ref lifecycle regression' and linked to INC-2026-224. assigning to eng-runtime/team.

sarah.k: next steps for SRE/eng-runtime: - hotfix: revert commit in 3.4.1 that altered KV ref clear path or backport fix to runtime-3.4.1-hotfix branch - add early eviction threshold when fragmentation > 0.8 - add metric: kv_slot_fragmentation_ratio and alert at 0.75 - stress test long-running streams with small allocations to reproduce slow leak

ajay: adding temporary runway: config flag 'kv_compact_on_threshold=true' to enable more frequent compaction on deployed nodes. will roll to dedicated pools.

lee: sending customer note template to cs for impacted tenants, flagging retries and degraded latency, cc:eng-runtime.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF in 30m to night oncall @lee — include link INC-2026-224 and RT-2026-881 in handoff.

sarah.k: leaving detailed thread notes in the incident page. i'll be available on pdt if needed. thanks team. :white_check_mark:

lee: acknowledged, monitoring dashboards and will escalate if any node shows >10% mem climb in 10m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT update — severity reduced to sev-2 after mitigation. continuing postmortem tracking.
